options.B: To immediately restore lost body weight and muscle mass
options.C: To avoid paying for extra unused medication refills
options.D: To guarantee permanent immunity against all respiratory viruses

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early allows the strongest bacteria to survive and mutate, making future infections much harder to cure. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h10)

question: What is the purpose of the spatula test when assessing for tetanus?

options.A: To clear respiratory secretions
options.B: To measure the core body temperature
options.C: To stimulate a normal gag reflex
options.D: To check for a reflex jaw spasm as a diagnostic sign

explanation: Touching the back of the mouth with a spatula causes reflex biting or jaw clamping in an infant with tetanus instead of a normal gag. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h4)

question: What happens inside a vestibular hair cell when its stereocilia bend toward the kinocilium?

options.A: Ion channels open and the cell depolarizes.
options.B: Potassium channels close and the cell dies.
options.C: Calcium crystals dissolve into the endolymph.
options.D: The cell releases stored digestive enzymes.

question: Why must nurses evaluate an IEC campaign even after distributing thousands of posters?

options.A: Printed paper naturally decays quickly in tropical weather conditions
options.B: Health clinics must justify their transport budgets to international donors
options.C: Government policy requires destroying old posters every six months
options.D: Distribution does not automatically mean the message changed health behaviors

explanation: Handing out materials is a logistical step, but true effectiveness is measured by sustained behavioral change. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is it necessary for nurse managers to understand national labour laws?

options.A: To write medical prescriptions for patients in outpatient clinics
options.B: To diagnose complex medical conditions in emergency wards
options.C: To protect employee rights and ensure fair institutional practices
options.D: To bypass the need for conducting job performance reviews

question: Why do many couples in local Nigerian settings prefer traditional family planning?

options.A: They are culturally familiar and cost-free
options.B: They require no active participation from partners
options.C: They provide protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: They have zero risk of unplanned pregnancy

question: What does a sampling frame represent in a research study?

options.A: The physical list used to select study participants
options.B: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.C: The final group of patients who complete the study
options.D: The theoretical group of all people with a condition

question: What immediate action must a nurse take upon finding a broken infusion pump?

options.A: Hide it inside a bedside locker until next week
options.B: Leave it plugged in for the next shift to discover
options.C: Tag it out of order and remove it from the active ward
options.D: Attempt to solder the internal circuit board alone

explanation: Immediate tagging and removal prevent accidental clinical use of a compromised device. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of anticoagulant drugs in the body?

options.A: Stimulating the production of platelets
options.B: Dissolving existing blood clots completely
options.C: Accelerating the normal healing of blood vessels
options.D: Preventing the formation of new blood clots

explanation: Anticoagulants stop the clotting process to keep new clots from forming or getting bigger. They do not dissolve clots that are already there; the body does that naturally. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h1)

question: Ancient Egyptian healing practices regarding diet were heavily focused on what concept?

options.A: Isolating pure vitamins
options.B: Counting macronutrients
options.C: Preventing bacterial infection
options.D: Purging and cleansing

explanation: Egyptians believed that removing excess food waste through purges and fasts maintained bodily purity and health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h2)

question: A patient has severe menstrual cramps, ongoing pelvic pain, and blocked fallopian tubes seen on an X-ray test. Which condition is the most likely cause?

options.A: Premature ovarian failure
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Uterine fibroids
options.D: Endometriosis

explanation: Endometriosis happens when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside of it, causing painful inflammation and scarring that can block the tubes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h3)

question: What is the primary pathophysiology underlying most types of glaucoma?

options.A: Clouding of the natural crystalline lens
options.B: Increased intraocular pressure damaging the optic nerve
options.C: Degeneration of the central macula on the retina
options.D: Bacterial infection of the anterior chamber

explanation: Glaucoma damages optic nerve fibers due to pressure buildup from trapped fluid within the eye. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h4)

question: What defines the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: The timeframe when antibiotics completely eliminate the microbe
options.B: The duration when specific rashes and fevers are peaking
options.C: The recovery phase where body tissues are finally repaired
options.D: The time from pathogen entry until first symptoms appear

explanation: Incubation is the silent phase between exposure and the onset of any clinical signs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h6)

question: Domestic burns among Nigerian teenagers are most often linked to which household factor?

options.A: Spontaneous combustion of synthetic bedding
options.B: Defective electric vehicle charging stations
options.C: Faulty central heating and radiator systems
options.D: Open-flame cooking and unsafe fuel handling

explanation: Using kerosene stoves and open fires creates a high risk for severe thermal injuries in the home. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h3)

question: When is the routine postnatal clinical assessment of the pelvic floor usually conducted?

options.A: Immediately after cord clamping
options.B: At twelve months postpartum

question: A nurse uses dietary assessment findings primarily to:

options.A: Prescribe long-term physical therapy routines

options.D: Determine the patient's exact discharge date

explanation: Assessment data directly informs patient education and tracks whether a prescribed medical diet is working. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h2)

question: What is a primary goal of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy in chronic degenerative illnesses?

options.A: Restoring full muscle strength and nerve function
options.B: Encouraging total denial of the physical symptoms
options.C: Restructuring negative thought patterns about the diagnosis
options.D: Eliminating the need for any pharmaceutical intervention

explanation: CBT focuses on identifying and changing harmful cognitive distortions, helping patients cope better with their changing reality. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h4)

question: Which practice directly threatens the survival of a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Adjusting drug prices to match wholesale inflation rates
options.B: Keeping clear financial records of all daily transactions
options.C: Conducting regular physical stock counts of all medicines
options.D: Extending unauthorized credit sales to staff and patients

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard food safety practice taught by community nurses?

options.A: Ensuring raw and cooked foods are kept separate
options.B: Practicing proper hand hygiene before cooking
options.C: Leaving cooked foods uncovered at room temperature for days
options.D: Using safe methods to protect food without refrigeration

question: Which procedure allows a doctor to look directly at the intestinal lining and take a tissue sample?

options.A: Urinalysis and culture
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Endoscopy with biopsy
options.D: Plain abdominal X-ray

explanation: Endoscopy allows direct visualization of the intestinal lining and retrieval of tissue samples for laboratory confirmation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is a standard nursing intervention to prevent pressure injuries in immobile residents?

options.A: Keeping room temperatures exceptionally warm
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to minimize skin moisture
options.C: Repositioning the resident every two hours
options.D: Applying adhesive tape firmly over bony prominences

question: Why do patients receiving chronic, repeated blood transfusions frequently develop iron overload?

options.A: Red blood cells break down and release iron into the kidneys

options.C: Transfusions stimulate excessive dietary iron absorption
options.D: The human body lacks an active mechanism to excrete excess iron

question: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is serum sickness?

options.A: Type II hypersensitivity reaction
options.B: Type I hypersensitivity reaction
options.C: Type IV hypersensitivity reaction
options.D: Type III hypersensitivity reaction

explanation: Serum sickness is caused by immune complexes building up in the body, which makes it a type III hypersensitivity reaction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why does the pulse wave travel down your arteries much faster than the actual blood flows?

options.A: Vascular resistance pushes fluid ahead of the cells
options.B: Red blood cells move faster during systole
options.C: Valves in the arteries accelerate fluid velocity
options.D: It travels as a pressure wave along elastic arterial walls

question: What is the main job of activated charcoal in the stomach and intestines?

options.A: To coat the intestines and speed up waste removal
options.B: To bind to toxins and stop them from entering the blood
options.C: To neutralize stomach acid
options.D: To cause vomiting

explanation: Activated charcoal catches poisons on its large surface, preventing them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h7)

question: Why is training displaced persons as health volunteers effective in camps?

options.A: They understand the local culture and language easily

options.C: They require no financial compensation at all

question: Which items are best suited for dry heat sterilization in an oven?

question: How can a home health nurse help prevent pressure injuries in a bedridden stroke patient?

options.B: Turn and reposition the patient every two hours

options.D: Keep the head of the bed elevated at 90 degrees

question: Why is a detailed psychosocial check important when treating an injured teenager?

options.A: Adolescents always report their emotional struggles during routine triage
options.B: Physical injuries in teenagers never heal properly without counseling
options.C: Hospital insurance policies strictly mandate psychiatric evaluations for minors
options.D: Many injuries stem from underlying behavioral risks or unreported violence

question: When is a nurse most expected to collect baseline anthropometric data?

options.A: Only during surgical procedures

question: What does micronutrient bioavailability measure?

options.D: The total weight of vitamins present in a raw food item

question: Which skin finding is most indicative of a low platelet count during a symptom review?

options.A: Cyanosis

question: What term describes an infection that is naturally transmitted from vertebrate animals to humans?

options.A: Iatrogenic infection

question: What is the primary purpose of menu planning in a hospital setting?

question: Which dietary nutrient is essential for the formation of the collagen matrix during bone healing?

question: What is the primary focus of epidemiology in community nursing?

options.A: Treating individual patients inside hospital wards

question: A patient is brought to the clinic, does not answer when called, but groans when pinched. Which triage level fits best?

question: Why is health education crucial during emergency disaster response in a community?
